source_text: Λίβανος δὲ καὶ ἅλας αὐτοῖς τὰ ἐπιπαττόμενα, τοῦ μὲν λιβάνου τὸ εὐῶδες ἐν ἁγιασμῷ, καὶ εὐωδίᾳ Χριστοῦ, τοῦ γε μὴν ἁλὸς, τὴν φρόνησιν ὑπεμφαίνοντος. Οὐ γὰρ ἀσύνετος ἢ μωρὸς τῶν ἁγίων ὁ λόγος, ἀλλ' ἐν χάριτί τε καὶ ἅλατι ἠρτυμένος, κατὰ τὸ γεγραμμένον, καὶ χάριν διδοὺς τοῖς ἀκούουσιν. Εἴρηται δὲ πρὸς αὐτοὺς καὶ παρὰ Χριστοῦ· «Ὑμεῖς ἐστε τὸ ἅλας τῆς γῆς.» Προτίθενται δὲ καὶ ἐν ἡμέρᾳ Σαββάτων. Ἡμέρα γὰρ ἀναδείξεως τῶν ἁγίων ἀποστόλων, ὁ τοῦ νοητοῦ Σαββάτου καιρὸς, τοῦτ' ἔστιν, ἡ Χριστοῦ παρουσία, ἣν ἐπείπερ οὐκ ἔγνωσαν οἱ ἐξ Ἰσραὴλ, ὁ Παῦλός φησι περὶ αὐτῶν, «Ἄρα ἀπολείπεται σαββατισμὸς τῷ λαῷ τοῦ Θεοῦ.» Οὐ γὰρ εἰσῆλθον εἰς τὴν κατάπαυσιν αὐτοῦ, τὴν πίστιν οὐ προσηκάμενοι. Σαββατισμὸς οὖν νοητὸς καὶ ἀληθὴς, ὁ τῆς τοῦ Σωτῆρος ἡμῶν ἐπιδημίας καιρός. Ἐν ὀφθαλμοῖς δὲ Θεοῦ τῶν ἄρτων ἡ πρόθεσις, καὶ μὴν καὶ ἐν ὀφθαλμοῖς Ἰσραήλ. «Προθήσετε γὰρ, φησὶ, τῇ ἡμέρᾳ τῶν Σαββάτων ἔναντι Κυρίου διὰ παντὸς, παρὰ τῶν υἱῶν Ἰσραήλ·» θεωμένου καὶ διηνεκῶς ἀξιοῦντος τοὺς ἁγίους ἐπισκοπῆς. «Ὀφθαλμοὶ γὰρ Κυρίου ἐπὶ δικαίους,» φησί. Τοῦ δὲ Ἰσραὴλ, ὡς προσέχειν αὐτοῖς ὀφείλοντος, καὶ οἱονεί πως ἐφιστῶντος τῆς διανοίας τὸν ὀφθαλμὸν, οὗ καὶ εἰς τύπον ἂν εἴη ὁ σωματικός. «Ἀλλ' ἔσται, φησὶν, Ἀαρὼν καὶ τοῖς υἱοῖς αὐτοῦ, καὶ φάγονται αὐτά.» Πρόκειται γὰρ ἡμῖν εἰς τροφὴν τὰ τῶν ἁγίων ἀποστόλων συγγράμματα, τοῖς ἐν πίστει δεδικαιωμένοις, ἁγίῳ τε καὶ ἱερῷ γένει, λαοῖς τοῖς εἰς περιποίησιν, καὶ ἐξειλεγμένοις, καὶ τῇ τοῦ ἁγίου Πνεύματος χάριτι κατακεχρισμένοις. {ΠΑΛΛ.} Εὖ ἔφης· συναινέσαιμι γὰρ ἄν. Ἀλλὰ τοῦ δὴ χάριν, οὐκ ἐν τοῖς Ἁγίοις τῶν ἁγίων, ἀλλ' ἐν τῇ πρώτῃ σκηνῇ τοῦ ἁγίου Βαπτιστοῦ, καὶ τῶν ἁγίων ἀποστόλων οἱ τύποι; {ΚΥΡ.} Πρῶτον μὲν ὅτι πολὺ τὸ μεσολαβοῦν, καὶ οὐκ ἐν οἷς ὁ Χριστὸς, καὶ τὰ τῶν ἁγίων κείσεται, ἀλλ' οἱονεί πως ἔξω καὶ ἐν μείοσιν. Ἐξῄρηται γὰρ καὶ ἀνὰ μέρος ἐστὶ τὰ τοῦ Θεοῦ, καὶ πολὺς τὰ ἀνθρώπινα διατειχίζει λόγος, ἀσύγκριτον ἐπιδεικνὺς τὴν τῶν φύσεων ἰδιότητα, καὶ τὴν τῆς εὐκλείας διαφοράν. Εἶτα ὅτι γεγόνασιν ἐξ Ἰουδαίων καὶ τῆς κατὰ νόμον λατρείας. Ταύτῃ τοι τόπος ὥσπερ αὐτοῖς ὁ πρέπων ἡ πρώτη σκηνὴ, ἐν ᾗ τὸ ἐν τύποις ἔκειτο τῶν καρπωμάτων θυσιαστήριον· ἢ οὐκ ἐξ αἵματος Ἰσραὴλ καὶ ἀπὸ σκηνῆς ὥσπερ τῆς πρώτης, ἡ τῶν ἁγίων μαθητῶν γέγονε κλῆσις; {ΠΑΛΛ.} Καὶ μάλα. {ΚΥΡ.} Ἔχοντος δὴ οὖν ἀποχρώντως ἡμῖν εὖ μάλα τοῦ περὶ τούτων λόγου, παροιστέον, εἰ δοκεῖ, τὴν τοῦ θεσπεσίου Παύλου φωνὴν, διατρανοῦσαν ἀστείως, τὸ ἐπί γε τῇ πρώτῃ καὶ τῇ δευτέρᾳ σκηνῇ μαρτύριον. Γράφει δὲ ὧδε· «Τούτων δὲ οὕτω κατεσκευασμένων
pass_a_gloss: [Cyril, continuing] Frankincense (λίβανος) and salt (ἅλας) [are] the things sprinkled upon (ἐπιπάσσω) them [the loaves]: the frankincense [signifying] the fragrant (εὐῶδες) in sanctification (ἁγιασμός) and in fragrance (εὐωδία) of Christ, the salt hinting (ὑπεμφαίνω) prudence/understanding (φρόνησις). For not unintelligent (ἀσύνετος) or foolish (μωρός) [is] the word (λόγος) of the saints, but seasoned (ἀρτύω) in grace (χάρις) and salt, according to the written [word], and giving grace to the hearers. It has been said to them also by Christ: 'You are the salt of the earth.' They are set out (προτίθημι) also on the day of Sabbaths. For the day of showing-forth/public appointment (ἀνάδειξις) of the holy apostles [is] the time (καιρός) of the intelligible/spiritual (νοητός) Sabbath, that is, the presence/coming (παρουσία) of Christ; which, since those from Israel did not know (γινώσκω) it, Paul says about them, 'So then there remains (ἀπολείπεται) a sabbath-rest (σαββατισμός) for the people of God.' For they did not enter into his rest (κατάπαυσις), not having accepted (προσίεμαι) the faith (πίστις). So the spiritual and true sabbath-rest [is] the time of the sojourn/coming-to-dwell (ἐπιδημία) of our Savior. In the eyes of God [is] the setting-out (πρόθεσις) of the loaves (ἄρτοι), and indeed in the eyes of Israel: 'For you shall set out, he says, on the day of the Sabbaths before the Lord continually (διὰ παντός), from (παρά + gen.) the sons of Israel' — [in God's eyes] he watching (θεάομαι) and continually deeming the saints worthy (ἀξιόω) of oversight/care (ἐπισκοπή): 'For the eyes of the Lord [are] upon the righteous,' he says; [in Israel's eyes] Israel as owing (ὀφείλω) to attend (προσέχω) to them and as it were setting (ἐφίστημι) the eye of the mind (διάνοια), of which the bodily [eye] would be a type (τύπος). 'But it shall be, he says, for Aaron and his sons, and they shall eat them.' For set before us for food (τροφή) are the writings (συγγράμματα) of the holy apostles, for those justified (δικαιόω) in faith, a holy and sacred (ἱερός) race (γένος), peoples for possession (περιποίησις), and chosen out (ἐκλέγω), and anointed (καταχρίω) by the grace of the Holy Spirit. PALL.: Well you said; for I would agree (συναινέω). But for what reason [are] not in the Holies of holies but in the first tent (σκηνή) the types of the holy Baptist and of the holy apostles? CYR.: First, because great [is] the intervening (μεσολαβέω), and not in [the place] where Christ [is] will the things of the saints also lie, but as it were outside and in lesser [things]. For the things of God are taken out/exalted (ἐξαιρέω) and apart (ἀνὰ μέρος), and a great reckoning/distance (λόγος) walls off (διατειχίζω) the human things, showing incomparable (ἀσύγκριτος) the peculiar property (ἰδιότης) of the natures (φύσεις) and the difference (διαφορά) of glory (εὔκλεια). Then, because they came from Jews and from the worship (λατρεία) according to law. Therefore the fitting (πρέπων) place for them, as it were, [is] the first tent, in which lay in types the altar (θυσιαστήριον) of burnt offerings (καρπώματα). Or was not the calling (κλῆσις) of the holy disciples from the blood of Israel and as it were from the first tent? PALL.: Very much so. CYR.: The account about these things holding sufficiently (ἀποχρώντως) and very well for us, one must bring forward (παροιστέον), if it seems good, the voice of the divine/inspired (θεσπέσιος) Paul, making clear (διατρανόω) elegantly (ἀστείως) the testimony (μαρτύριον) concerning the first and the second tent. He writes thus: 'These things having been thus prepared (κατασκευάζω)…' [quotation runs on into §18].
pass_b_english: Cyril: Frankincense and salt are sprinkled on the loaves (Leviticus 24:7). The frankincense points to the sweet fragrance of sanctification and to the fragrance of Christ (2 Corinthians 2:15); the salt hints at understanding. For the word of the saints is not senseless or foolish but, as it is written, seasoned with grace and salt (Colossians 4:6), and it gives grace to those who hear (Ephesians 4:29). Christ also said to them, ‘You are the salt of the earth’ (Matthew 5:13). The loaves are set out on the Sabbath day as well (Leviticus 24:8). For the day on which the holy apostles were made known is the time of the spiritual Sabbath, that is, the coming of Christ. Because those of Israel did not recognize it, Paul says of them, ‘So then there remains a Sabbath rest for the people of God’ (Hebrews 4:9). For they did not enter into his rest, because they did not accept faith (Hebrews 3:18–19). The spiritual and true Sabbath rest, then, is the time when our Savior came to dwell among us. The loaves are set out before the eyes of God, and indeed before the eyes of Israel as well. For ‘you shall set them out,’ he says, ‘on the Sabbath day before the Lord continually, from the sons of Israel’ (Leviticus 24:8). They are before the eyes of God, because he looks on the saints and continually counts them worthy of his care; for ‘the eyes of the Lord are on the righteous,’ it says (Psalm 34:15). They are before the eyes of Israel, because Israel ought to give heed to them and, as it were, fixes on them the eye of the mind, of which the bodily eye would be a type. ‘But they shall belong,’ he says, ‘to Aaron and to his sons, and they shall eat them’ (Leviticus 24:9). For the writings of the holy apostles are set before us as food: before us who have been justified in faith, a holy and sacred race, peoples for his own possession (1 Peter 2:9), chosen and anointed with the grace of the Holy Spirit.
Palladius: Well said; I would agree. But why are the types of the holy Baptist and of the holy apostles not in the Holy of Holies but in the first tent?

Cyril: First, because the distance between them is great, and what belongs to the saints will not be placed where Christ is, but, as it were, outside and in a lesser place. For the things of God are set apart and stand by themselves, and a wide distance walls off what is human, showing that the distinct character of the natures and the difference in glory admit no comparison. Second, because they came from the Jews and from the worship under the law. For this reason the first tent is, so to speak, the place fitting for them, the tent in which stood the altar of burnt offerings, one of the types. Or did the calling of the holy disciples not come from the blood of Israel and, as it were, from the first tent?

Cyril: Since our account of these things is now well and sufficiently settled, we should bring in, if you agree, the voice of the inspired Paul, which sets out clearly and elegantly the testimony concerning the first and the second tent. He writes as follows: ‘Now when these things had been prepared in this way,…’ (Hebrews 9:6)

apparatus.note: PG OCR; column may cut mid-sentence.

Section opens mid-turn: Cyril's speech continues from §16 (no speaker mark in the source row), so it is labelled 'Cyril:'. Leviticus 24:7: the salt on the loaves comes from the Septuagint, which adds καὶ ἅλα to the frankincense; the Hebrew has frankincense only. Leviticus 24:8: the printed quotation reads παρὰ τῶν υἱῶν Ἰσραήλ ('from the sons of Israel'), where the Septuagint has ἐνώπιον τῶν υἱῶν Ἰσραήλ ('before the sons of Israel'); Cyril's comment ('before the eyes of Israel') presupposes the Septuagint wording. The English follows the printed text in the quotation; a reviewer may prefer to restore 'before'. Psalm 34:15 = LXX Psalm 33:16 (also quoted in 1 Peter 3:12). 2 Corinthians 2:15 cited for 'fragrance of Christ' (Χριστοῦ εὐωδία); Ephesians 4:29 for 'gives grace to those who hear' (ἵνα δῷ χάριν τοῖς ἀκούουσιν), combined with Colossians 4:6 under 'as it is written'. Hebrews 3:18–19 cited for 'they did not enter His rest ... because of unbelief'; Hebrews 4:6 is a close alternative. Uncited possible allusions: ἀνάδειξις ('public appearing') may echo Luke 1:80; 'justified in faith' (Romans 5:1) and 'anointed with the grace of the Spirit' (2 Corinthians 1:21; 1 John 2:20) are too general to cite. 'Peoples for His own possession': λαοῖς τοῖς εἰς περιποίησιν, plural, from 1 Peter 2:9; 'His' supplies the implied owner as the English Bible versions do. 'A wide difference': πολὺς λόγος here means a great measure or distance, not 'word'. The altar 'of burnt offerings' (τῶν καρπωμάτων) is placed by Cyril in the first tent; in Exodus 40:6, 29 that altar stands before the door of the tent. Translated as printed, no correction. Hebrews is quoted as Paul's, as Cyril holds. The Hebrews 9:6 quotation is cut at the column break (PG 68.681/684) and continues in §18. Reviewer: ἐφιστῶντος is parallel to ὀφείλοντος (Israel ought to attend and, as it were, fixes the mind's eye), not governed by 'ought'; ἀσύγκριτον governs both the distinct character of the natures and the difference in glory; Εἶτα ὅτι γεγόνασιν has the Baptist and the apostles together as subject ('they'). Lev 24:8 παρά kept as printed (see above).

changes: ἡμέρα ἀναδείξεως: 'public appearing' -> 'the day on which the holy apostles were made known'
Modality fixed: ἐφιστῶντος parallel to ὀφείλοντος, so Israel 'fixes' the mind's eye (not 'ought to fix')
'the things of the saints will not lie ... among lesser things' -> natural 'will not be placed ... in a lesser place'
ἀσύγκριτον now governs both the natures' distinct character and the difference in glory (was split)
Εἶτα ὅτι γεγόνασιν: subject 'the apostles' -> 'they' (Baptist and apostles together)
Calque 'the altar of burnt offerings stood in types' -> 'stood the altar of burnt offerings, one of the types'
Hebrews 9:6 opening 'these things having been so prepared' -> 'when these things had been prepared in this way'

Checked citations: Leviticus 24:7 (LXX adds salt), 2 Corinthians 2:15, Colossians 4:6, Ephesians 4:29, Matthew 5:13, Leviticus 24:8, Hebrews 4:9, Hebrews 3:18-19, Psalm 34:15 (LXX 33:16), Leviticus 24:9, 1 Peter 2:9, Hebrews 9:6: all correct
